QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_11

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short posted sub-period returns of +5%, -2%, +8%, +3% in four consecutive quarters. What is the annual Time-Weighted Return (TWR) for the year?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** TWR = (1.05)(0.98)(1.08)(1.03) − 1 = 1.05 × 0.98 × 1.08 × 1.03 = 1.14448... − 1 ≈ 14.45%. TWR neutralises the effect of mid-period cash flows and is the industry-standard metric for comparing manager skill across funds. **The Trap:** 14.00% is simple arithmetic sum. 3.50% is the arithmetic average. 14.55% rounds wrong. **Cross-Exam Context:** GIPS standards (referenced in the chapter) mandate TWR for performance reporting. XIX-C All-Cat Manager tests TWR too; XIX-E tests it Cat III-specific. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** TWR requires daily NAV and revaluation on every external cash flow. Ensure fund admin books subscription/redemption on the FOLLOWING business day (dealing day) to avoid stale-NAV arbitrage by sophisticated LPs.
